newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-UNBEATEN PORTO CRUISE TO QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNBEATEN PORTO CRUISE TO QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Porto, already guaranteed a European Cup quarter-final place, sealed their supremacy in their Champions' League group with a 2-0 win over Gothenburg on Wednesday.
The Portuguese champions topped Group D with 16 points, seven more than second-placed Rosenborg of Norway, after winning five of their six matches with their fluid football.

The Swedes, who went into the game with no chance of reaching the last eight, looked lethargic. The Swedish season ended last month and midfielder Jesper Blomqvist was Gothenburg's only success on a cold, wet and windy night.

Blomqvist will fly out of Sweden on Thursday to join AC Milan, whose European campaign ended as disastrously as Gothenburg's with defeat by Rosenborg in their make-or-break clash in the San Siro stadium.

But Wednesday belonged to Porto's talented Brazilians. Mario Jardel, who scored twice when his team beat Milan 3-2 in their opening Champions' League match in September, broke the deadlock in the 64th minute after a dull and featureless first hour.
Jardel soared above the Gothenburg defence to head powerfully home from a cross of pinpoint accuracy from compatriot Artur, a substitute who also played a key role in Porto's second goal.
Porto pressed home the advantage, pinning the Swedes in their own half for the rest of the match while goalkeeper Henrique Hilario shivered in several layers of clothing with nothing to do.
Artur, who replaced Fernando Mendes at halftime, played a perfect through ball to midfielder Edmilson Pimenta, another Brazilian, one minute before the end of the game.
Edmilson drove past international goalkeeper Thomas Ravelli to secure an easy victory.
Porto coach Antonio Oliveira blamed the Portuguese club's slow start on the cold and greasy conditions.
"It was slippery and it took us an entire half to get going but apart from that we played pretty well," he said.

Gothenburg: 1-Thomas Ravelli; 4-Jonas Olsson, 6-Teddy Lucic, 8-Peter Eriksson, 10-Stefan Pettersson; 11-Stefan Lindqvist, 13-Mikael Nilsson, 14-Andreas Andersson, 16-Jesper Blomqvist; 19-Magnus Erlingmark, 22-Stefan Landberg (3-Magnus Johansson, 18).

Porto: 24-Henrique Hilario; 4-Aloisio Alves, 5-Fernando Mendes (14-Artur 45), 7-Sergio Conceicao, 11-Ljubinko Drulovic; 16-Mario Jardel (8-Rui Barros 80), 17-Jose Barroso, 19-Joao Manuel Pinto, 20-Paulinho Santos; 21-Edmilson Pimenta, 25-Zlatko Zahovic.
